question: When checking the engine oil level during the pre-trip inspection, what must be true about the oil level?
choice_a: It must be above the refill mark on the dipstick, checked with the engine off
choice_b: It must be below the refill mark to prevent overfilling
choice_c: It must be checked while the engine is running at idle
choice_d: It must be checked only using the sight glass
explanation: The manual states you check oil level when the engine is off, and the level must be above the refill mark on the dipstick.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Engine Compartment Oil Level

question: How should you check the coolant level during a pre-trip engine compartment inspection, according to the Wyoming CDL manual?
choice_a: Remove the radiator cap when the engine is hot to check the level directly
choice_b: Look at the sight glass on the radiator or coolant reservoir; an adequate level will show in the sight glass
choice_c: Check the coolant using the same dipstick as the engine oil
choice_d: Coolant level cannot be inspected without lifting the vehicle
explanation: The manual instructs looking at the sight glass on the radiator or coolant reservoir, and cautions never to remove the radiator cap when the engine is hot.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Coolant Level

question: During the engine compartment inspection, where should the power steering fluid level be relative to the refill mark?
choice_a: At or below the add mark
choice_b: It doesn't matter as long as there are no leaks
choice_c: Above the refill mark, checked via dipstick or sight glass
choice_d: Exactly at the midpoint between add and full
explanation: The manual states the power steering fluid level must be above the refill mark, checked via the dipstick or sight glass.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Power Steering Fluid

question: When inspecting the engine compartment belts (power steering, water pump, alternator, air compressor), what amount of play at the center of the belt indicates proper snugness?
choice_a: No play at all (belt should be completely rigid)
choice_b: 1/4 to 1/2 inch
choice_c: 1 to 2 inches
choice_d: 1/2 to 3/4 inch
explanation: The manual specifies checking belts for snugness with 1/2 to 3/4 inch play at the center of the belt, along with cracks or frays.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Engine Compartment Belts

question: If one of the engine compartment components (such as the water pump or air compressor) is not belt driven, what must you do during the inspection?
choice_a: Tell the examiner which component(s) are not belt driven and confirm they are operating properly, not damaged/leaking, and mounted securely
choice_b: Skip mentioning it since it doesn't apply
choice_c: Automatically fail the vehicle inspection test
choice_d: Ask the examiner to substitute a different vehicle
explanation: The manual's note instructs that for non-belt-driven components, you must tell the examiner which components are not belt driven and confirm they operate properly, are not damaged or leaking, and are mounted securely.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Engine Compartment Belts note

topic: Hydraulic brakes - master cylinder and fluid
question: For a vehicle with hydraulic brakes, what must you check regarding the master cylinder and brake fluid during the engine compartment inspection?
choice_a: That the master cylinder is empty prior to starting
choice_b: That the master cylinder is securely attached and not leaking, and that brake fluid is between the add and full marks
choice_c: That the master cylinder has been replaced within the last year
choice_d: That brake fluid is at the very top of the reservoir, above the full mark
explanation: The manual requires checking that the master cylinder is securely attached and not leaking, and that the brake fluid level in the reservoir is between the add and full marks.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Hydraulic Brakes Master Cylinder & Brake Fluid

question: What is part of the correct safe starting procedure listed in the Wyoming CDL manual?
choice_a: Leave the gearshift in reverse before starting to confirm it engages
choice_b: Rev the engine immediately to full throttle after starting
choice_c: Place the gearshift in neutral (or park for automatic transmissions) and depress the clutch before attempting to start the vehicle
choice_d: Release the clutch immediately once the engine turns over, before it reaches idle
explanation: The Safe Start procedure requires placing the gearshift lever in neutral (or park for automatic transmissions) and depressing the clutch before attempting to start the vehicle, keeping it depressed until idling speed, then releasing slowly.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Safe Start

question: During the cab check after engine start, what should you verify about the oil pressure gauge?
choice_a: It should read zero until the vehicle reaches highway speed
choice_b: It is not required to be checked if a warning light is present
choice_c: It should show maximum pressure immediately
choice_d: It is working and shows increasing or normal oil pressure, or that the warning light goes off
explanation: The manual requires confirming the oil pressure gauge is working and shows increasing or normal oil pressure, or that the warning light goes off.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Cab Check/Engine Start, Oil Pressure Gauge

question: What should the temperature gauge do shortly after the engine starts, per the cab check procedure?
choice_a: Begin to climb toward the normal operating range, or the temperature warning light should go off
choice_b: Stay at zero until the vehicle has been driven 10 miles
choice_c: Immediately show a high-temperature warning
choice_d: Drop to below the normal range
explanation: The manual states the temperature should begin to climb to the normal operating range, or the temperature light should be off.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Cab Check/Engine Start, Temperature Gauge

topic: Cab check - air gauge and governor cut-out
question: When checking the air gauge during the cab check, the air compressor should build air pressure to a governor cut-out of approximately what range, per the Wyoming CDL manual?
explanation: The manual states the air compressor should build air pressure to governor cut-out at approximately 120-140 psi or as specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Cab Check/Engine Start, Air Gauge

question: What does checking the ammeter/voltmeter gauge during the cab check confirm?
choice_a: The engine oil level
choice_b: The transmission fluid temperature
choice_c: That the alternator and/or generator is charging, or that the warning light is off
choice_d: The tire pressure of all axles
explanation: The manual states you check that the gauges show the alternator and/or generator is charging or that the warning light is off.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Cab Check/Engine Start, Ammeter/Voltmeter

question: According to the modernized (11M) inspection description, what is the ONE item allowed to be on the windshield without being considered damage or an obstruction?
choice_a: A parking permit
choice_b: A tinted visor strip
choice_c: A dealer advertisement decal
choice_d: An inspection sticker
explanation: Section 11M states to inspect that the windshield is clean with no obstructions except for an inspection sticker, and that there is no damage such as cracks or flaws to the glass.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11M - Windshield and Traffic Monitoring Devices

question: What emergency equipment must a CDL vehicle carry, per the Wyoming CDL manual's emergency equipment inspection?
choice_a: Three red reflective triangles and six fuses or three liquid burning flares
choice_b: Two red reflective triangles and four fuses
choice_c: One reflective triangle and a set of jumper cables
choice_d: Five liquid burning flares only
explanation: The manual requires checking for three red reflective triangles and 6 fuses or 3 liquid burning flares as part of the emergency equipment check.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Emergency Equipment

question: What must be verified about the fire extinguisher during the emergency equipment inspection?
choice_a: That it is empty and due for replacement
choice_b: That it is properly charged, rated, and securely mounted
choice_c: That it is stored in the trailer only
choice_d: That it has a valid inspection date within the past week
explanation: The manual requires checking that the fire extinguisher is properly charged, rated and securely mounted.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Emergency Equipment

question: During the wipers/washers inspection, what must you confirm besides the wiper arms and blades being secure and undamaged?
choice_a: That the wipers are replaced with a new set before testing
choice_b: That the washer fluid is colored blue
choice_c: That, if equipped, the windshield washers operate correctly
choice_d: That the wipers only operate on the highest speed setting
explanation: The manual states that wiper arms and blades must be secure, not damaged, and operate smoothly, and that if equipped, windshield washers must operate correctly.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Wipers/Washers

question: Which of the following is included in the list of dash indicators that must be tested to correspond with their lights during the internal inspection?
choice_a: Cruise control indicator
choice_b: Odometer reading
choice_c: Fuel gauge sender
choice_d: Antilock Braking System (ABS) indicator
explanation: The manual lists testing that dash indicators work when corresponding lights are turned on, including left turn signal, right turn signal, four-way emergency flashers, high-beam headlight, and the ABS indicator.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Lights/Reflectors/Reflector Tape Condition

question: Per the light and reflector check requirements, what color must clearance lights be on the rear of the vehicle versus elsewhere?
choice_a: Red on the rear, amber elsewhere
choice_b: Amber on the rear, red elsewhere
choice_c: White on the rear, blue elsewhere
choice_d: All clearance lights must be amber regardless of location
explanation: The manual lists clearance lights as red on the rear and amber elsewhere as part of the lights/reflectors check.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Lights/Reflectors

question: What must be verified regarding the horn during the pre-trip inspection?
choice_a: That only the electric horn functions, since air horns are prohibited
choice_b: That the air horn and/or electric horn work
choice_c: That the horn produces a minimum of 90 decibels as measured by a meter
choice_d: That the horn is disconnected for the duration of the test
explanation: The manual simply requires checking that the air horn and/or electric horn work.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Horn

question: What must be tested regarding cab comfort/visibility systems, per the pre-trip inspection?
choice_a: The radio and air conditioning
choice_b: Only the defroster, not the heater
choice_c: That the heater and defroster work
choice_d: The cruise control system
explanation: The manual requires testing that the heater and defroster work; the 11M version notes the defroster improves visibility especially during cold weather.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Heater/Defroster

question: On a combination vehicle, how do you check that the parking brake will hold the vehicle, per the parking brake check procedure?
choice_a: Drive forward at 5 mph and brake suddenly
choice_b: Release all brakes and coast down a hill
choice_c: Check only the trailer's electronic brake controller readout
choice_d: With air pressure built to governor cutout and the parking brake engaged (trailer brakes released), gently try to pull forward with the parking brake on
explanation: The manual states that with air pressure built to governor cutout and the parking brake engaged (trailer brakes released on combination vehicles), you check that the parking brake will hold the vehicle by gently trying to pull forward with the parking brake on.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Parking Brake Check

question: What is the correct procedure for the hydraulic brake pedal check during the pre-trip inspection?
choice_a: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds; the pedal should not move (depress) during those five seconds
choice_b: Pump the brake pedal ten times rapidly and release immediately
choice_c: Hold the brake pedal down for thirty seconds without pumping first
choice_d: Press the brake pedal once and immediately restart the engine
explanation: The manual instructs pumping the brake pedal three times, then holding it down for five seconds, during which the pedal should not move (depress).
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Hydraulic Brake Check

question: During the air leakage rate test with the engine shut off and the foot brake fully applied and held for one minute, what is the maximum allowable air pressure drop for a single vehicle?
choice_a: 1 pound
choice_b: 3 pounds
choice_c: 6 pounds
choice_d: 10 pounds
explanation: The manual states the air pressure should not drop more than three pounds in one minute for a single vehicle (or four pounds for a combination vehicle).
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Air Brake Check / Section 11M Air Leakage Rate Test

topic: Air brake check - low air warning
question: As you fan off air pressure during the air brake warning device test, the low air warning devices (buzzer, light, flag) should activate before the air pressure drops below approximately what level?
choice_a: 80 psi
choice_b: 100 psi
choice_c: 55 psi
choice_d: 20 psi
explanation: The manual states the low air warning devices should activate before air pressure drops below 55 psi or the level specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Air Brake Check / Section 11M Air Warning Device(s) Test

topic: Air brake check - emergency brake valve pop-out
question: Per the modernized (11M) air brake check, the emergency brake (parking brake) valve should close (pop out) within what psi range?
choice_a: 60 to 80 psi
choice_b: 10 to 15 psi
choice_c: 0 to 10 psi
choice_d: 20 to 45 psi (no less than 20 psi and no more than 45 psi)
explanation: Section 11M's Emergency Brake(s) Test states the parking brake (or emergency brake) valve should close (pop out) between 20 psi and 45 psi.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11M - Emergency Brake(s) Test

question: What happens if a CDL applicant fails to perform the air brake check correctly during the vehicle inspection test?
choice_a: It results in an automatic failure of the vehicle inspection test
choice_b: The examiner simply notes it and continues the test
choice_c: The applicant is given a written warning and may retake only that portion
choice_d: It only affects the score if the vehicle is a combination vehicle
explanation: The manual states that failure to perform an air brake check will result in an automatic failure of the vehicle inspection test.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Air Brake Check

question: How is the service brake check performed during the pre-trip/vehicle inspection test?
choice_a: Accelerate to 20 mph and slam the brakes
choice_b: Pull forward at 5 mph, apply the service brake, and stop, checking that the vehicle does not pull to either side
choice_c: Apply the parking brake only while stationary
choice_d: Check the brakes only while the vehicle is in reverse
explanation: The manual instructs pulling forward at 5 mph, applying the service brake, and stopping, checking that the vehicle does not pull to either side and that it stops when the brake is applied.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Service Brake Check

question: What must you check regarding the safety belt during the pre-trip inspection?
choice_a: That it automatically retracts within two seconds
choice_b: That it is a five-point harness system
choice_c: That it is securely mounted, adjusts and latches properly, and is not ripped or frayed
choice_d: That it has been replaced within the last 12 months
explanation: The manual requires checking that the safety belt is securely mounted, adjusts, and latches properly and is not ripped or frayed.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Safety Belt

question: During the external steering inspection, what must you check about the steering box?
choice_a: That it is painted the same color as the frame
choice_b: That it has been recently lubricated within the past week
choice_c: That it is mounted with exactly four bolts
choice_d: That it is securely mounted and not leaking, with no missing nuts and/or bolts
explanation: The manual requires checking that the steering box is securely mounted and not leaking, and looking for any missing nuts and/or bolts.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Steering Box/Hoses

question: What must you inspect regarding the steering linkage (connecting links, arms, and rods from the steering box to the wheel)?
choice_a: That they are not worn or cracked, and that joints/sockets are not worn or loose with no missing nuts, bolts, or cotter keys
choice_b: That they are painted with rust-proof coating
choice_c: That they are replaced every 50,000 miles
choice_d: That they are covered with a protective boot at all times
explanation: The manual states to see that connecting links, arms, and rods are not worn or cracked, and that joints and sockets are not worn or loose with no missing nuts, bolts, or cotter keys.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Steering Linkage

question: When inspecting the suspension, what should you look for regarding leaf springs?
choice_a: That they are painted black
choice_b: Missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs
choice_c: That they are the original manufacturer's springs only
choice_d: That they make no noise when driven over
explanation: The manual instructs looking for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs as part of the suspension inspection.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Springs/Air/Torque

question: What should you look for when inspecting the suspension mounts (spring hangers, bushings, u-bolts)?
choice_a: Only visible rust discoloration
choice_b: Whether they are painted a factory-matched color
choice_c: Cracked or broken spring hangers, missing or damaged bushings, and broken, loose, or missing bolts/u-bolts
choice_d: The manufacturer's date stamp
explanation: The manual requires looking for cracked or broken spring hangers, missing or damaged bushings, and broken, loose, or missing bolts, u-bolts or other axle mounting parts.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Mounts

question: What must you check regarding the shock absorbers during the suspension inspection?
choice_a: That they are the same brand on every axle
choice_b: That they are less than one year old
choice_c: That they bounce the vehicle at least three times when pressed
choice_d: That they are secure and there are no leaks
explanation: The manual states to see that shock absorbers are secure and that there are no leaks.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Shock Absorbers

question: For manual slack adjustors, how much should the brake pushrod move (with brakes released) when pulled by hand, per the Wyoming CDL manual?
choice_a: Not more than one inch
choice_b: Not more than six inches
choice_c: It should not move at all, even slightly
choice_d: Up to three inches is acceptable
explanation: The manual states that for manual slack adjustors, the brake pushrod should not move more than one inch (with the brakes released) when pulled by hand.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Slack Adjustors and Pushrods

question: What must you check about the brake chambers during the brakes inspection?
choice_a: That they are painted red for visibility
choice_b: That they are not leaking, cracked, or dented and are mounted securely
choice_c: That they are replaced every time the vehicle is inspected
choice_d: That they contain hydraulic fluid
explanation: The manual requires seeing that brake chambers are not leaking, cracked, or dented and are mounted securely.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Brake Chambers

question: During the brakes inspection, what should you look for regarding brake hoses, lines, and couplings?
choice_a: That they are the same length on every axle
choice_b: That they are colored differently from air lines
choice_c: Cracked, worn, or leaking hoses, lines, and couplings
choice_d: That they are made of rubber only, never metal
explanation: The manual instructs looking for cracked, worn, or leaking brake hoses, lines, and couplings.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Brake Hoses/Lines

question: What should you inspect on a drum brake during the pre-trip inspection?
choice_a: The paint finish on the drum exterior
choice_b: The manufacturer's serial number stamped on the drum
choice_c: The drum's total weight
choice_d: Cracks, dents, or holes; loose or missing bolts; and contaminates such as debris or oil/grease
explanation: The manual requires checking the drum brake for cracks, dents, or holes, loose or missing bolts, and contaminates such as debris or oil/grease.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Drum Brake

question: On brake drums with openings that allow the brake linings to be seen from outside the drum, what must you check?
choice_a: That a visible amount of brake lining is showing
choice_b: That the lining is a specific brand
choice_c: That no lining at all is visible, indicating full wear
choice_d: That the lining has been recently painted
explanation: The manual states that for drum types with viewing openings, you check that a visible amount of brake lining is showing.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Brake Linings

question: What is stated about welding repairs on rims during the wheels inspection?
choice_a: Welding repairs are acceptable if performed by a certified welder
choice_b: Rims cannot have welding repairs
choice_c: Welding repairs are only prohibited on steering axle rims
choice_d: Welding repairs must be inspected annually but are otherwise allowed
explanation: The manual explicitly states that rims cannot have welding repairs, in addition to checking for damaged or bent rims and rust trails.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Rims

question: What is the minimum tread depth requirement checked during the tire inspection, per the Wyoming CDL manual?
choice_a: 2/32 on steering axle tires, 4/32 on all other tires
choice_b: 6/32 on all tires
choice_c: 4/32 on steering axle tires, 2/32 on all other tires
choice_d: 8/32 on steering axle tires, 4/32 on all other tires
explanation: The manual requires checking for minimum tread depth of 4/32 on steering axle tires and 2/32 on all other tires.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Tires, Tread Depth

question: How must tire inflation be checked during the pre-trip inspection, and what will NOT earn credit?
choice_a: By listening for a hissing sound; a stethoscope is acceptable
choice_b: By visual estimation alone; no tool is required
choice_c: By weighing the vehicle on a scale
choice_d: By using a tire gauge; you will not get credit for simply kicking the tires or using a mallet
explanation: The manual requires checking tire inflation by using a tire gauge, and specifically notes you will not get credit for kicking the tires or using a mallet to check inflation.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Tires, Tire Inflation

question: What must you check about lug nuts during the wheels inspection?
choice_a: That all lug nuts are present, free of cracks and distortions, and show no signs of looseness such as rust trails or shiny threads
choice_b: That they are torqued to exactly 100 ft-lbs using a torque wrench during the test
choice_c: That there are no more than two missing per wheel
choice_d: That they are chrome-plated
explanation: The manual requires checking that all lug nuts are present, free of cracks and distortions, and show no signs of looseness such as rust trails or shiny threads.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Lug Nuts

question: What must you inspect regarding the drive shaft during the side-of-vehicle inspection?
choice_a: That it is painted to match the frame
choice_b: That it is not bent or cracked, and that couplings are secure and free of foreign objects
choice_c: That it has been replaced within the warranty period
choice_d: That it produces no vibration above 60 mph
explanation: The manual requires seeing that the drive shaft is not bent or cracked, and that couplings are secure and free of foreign objects.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Drive Shaft

topic: Side of vehicle - DEF tank level
question: For a vehicle equipped with emissions after-treatment equipment, what must you check about the DEF (diesel exhaust fluid) tank level?
choice_a: That it is completely full at all times
choice_b: That it is empty before starting the test
choice_c: That the level of diesel exhaust fluid in the tank is adequate, meaning more than 1/8th tank
choice_d: That it has been refilled within the last 24 hours
explanation: The manual states that if equipped with emissions after-treatment equipment, you check the DEF tank to ensure the level of diesel exhaust fluid is adequate, meaning more than 1/8th tank.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Exhaust System, DEF Tank

question: When inspecting a fifth wheel coupling system, what must you check by looking into the fifth wheel gap?
choice_a: That the fifth wheel is a specific manufacturer brand
choice_b: That the kingpin has been replaced within the last year
choice_c: That the trailer height matches the tractor height exactly
choice_d: That the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin
explanation: The manual instructs looking into the fifth wheel gap and checking that the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Locking Jaws (Fifth Wheel) / Section 11M Fifth Wheel Coupling Systems

question: When inspecting the air and electric lines at the tractor/trailer coupling, what should you check regarding the air hoses and electrical lines?
choice_a: That they are not cut, chafed, spliced, or worn, with steel braid not showing through, and are not tangled, pinched, or dragging against parts
choice_b: That they are exactly six feet in length
choice_c: That they are color-coded red and blue only
choice_d: That they are disconnected during the pre-trip inspection for safety
explanation: The manual requires listening for air leaks and checking that air hoses and electrical lines are not cut, chafed, spliced, or worn (steel braid should not show through), and are not tangled, pinched, or dragging against tractor parts.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 11 - Tractor/Coupling, Air/Electric Lines
